title: ux-metric-sleuth-standup-notes-2027-10-29
content:
Date: 2027-10-29
Owner: Claire Donovan (notes)
Attendees: Claire, Samir, Jonah, Priya, Marta (partial)
Context: quick followup from yesterday's alert run — rolling canary for panel rollout showed a 12-18% spike in per-route 95th latency for routes handling `panel-render` when active-user concurrency > 220. This surfaced after the new analytics-payload change merged in PR 2987.

Agenda:
- Triage the latency spike and isolate whether it's client-side rendering, backend aggregation, or a telemetry artifact
- Decide immediate canary action (pause/rollback/patch)
- Plan short experiment to surface root cause and measure impact
- Assign owners for follow-up instrumentation and a small mitigation patch

Quick notes / findings so far:
- Canary timeline: rolled at 04:10 UTC, alerts triggered 04:36 UTC, full rollback started 05:05 UTC.
- A/B breakdown shows the spike only when analytics payloads include `session_features=v2` (new format) and when downstream aggregators coalesce events into the 15s batching window.
- Frontend sampling shows no DOM-heavy regressions; CPU on client machines nominal. Chrome trace for 2 users shows network tail latencies aligned with service-side tokenization stage.
- Panel-render route logs show 2x increase in time spent in `analytics-serializer` in the service trace during spike window (avg went from 8ms -> 22ms).
- KV cache hit rate unchanged. Batching size distributions shifted (median batch size for aggregator increased from 3 -> 7 in the canary cohort).

Hypothesis (ranked):
1) New analytics payload format caused larger serialized messages which push aggregator batching behavior into a less efficient path (aggregation overhead + serialization cost) -> server-side CPU/GC pressure -> higher tail latency.
2) Instrumentation mismatch: our UX telemetry pipeline re-annotates traces and accidentally adds synchronous I/O in the hot path under certain payload shapes.
3) Downstream DB writes had a narrow window of backpressure coincidentally aligned with canary; less likely given no errors in DB metrics.

Immediate decision (live):
- Pause canary and revert rollout flag for panel rollout in canary cohort at 05:10 UTC (owner: Samir).
- Keep non-canary cohorts stable. No full rollout until mitigation validated.

Action items (owners, ETA):
- Samir: Reproduce locally with a synthetic runner that emits `session_features=v2` payloads and measures `analytics-serializer` per-request timing. ETA: 2027-10-30 EOD.
- Jonah: Add fine-grained timers around serializer + aggregator enqueue path and push a short-lived debug build to the staging canary group (feature flag). Also capture allocator/GC stats. ETA: 2027-10-30 noon.
- Priya: Prepare a quick patch that optimizes serializer by switching to faster binary encoding for `v2` sessions (prototype branch `opt/ser-v2`). Measure perf delta. ETA: 2027-11-01.
- Marta: Verify that downstream aggregator batching thresholds didn't change in deploys. Check config drift across regions. ETA: 2027-10-30 morning.
- Claire: Draft post-mortem skeleton and update the canary playbook with this incident's checks (add `serializer duration` and `batch size distribution` to canary SLOs). ETA: 2027-11-02.

Instrumentation & observability tasks:
- Add a new derived metric: `panel_render.serializer_p95_by_payload_shape` (Jonah + Samir). Aim: surface regressions by payload shape within dashboards and Alerting.
- Temp dashboard tiles to compare `batch_size_histogram` and `serializer_latencies` side-by-side for canary vs baseline. Use short retention (14 days) and link into the canary view.
- Add a short-lived trace sampling rule for `panel-render` with `session_features=v2` to 100% for 1 hour during tests.

Experiment plan (small, measurable steps):
1) Reproduce: synthetic runner + debug build to ensure serializer is dominant. If reproducible -> go to step 2.
2) Patch: apply `opt/ser-v2` and measure delta in staging canary (goal: reduce serializer p95 by >= 40%).
3) Canary run: re-enable rollout on 5% of users with enhanced monitoring and a rollback within 30 minutes if p95 rises > 10% from baseline.
4) If patch not sufficient, fallback is to revert payload to `session_features=v1` (compatibility shim) while longer-term serializer optimization proceeds.

Risk & mitigation notes:
- Risk: Shimming back to `v1` for a portion of users may trigger mismatch bugs in analytics consumers. Mitigation: add translation layer server-side that converts `v2` -> `v1` for canary cohort only; add end-to-end validation in the pipeline.
- Risk: Debug build may increase tail latency artificially; tests should run during low-traffic windows and compare against controlled baseline.

Loose checklist / quick wins:
- [x] Pause canary / flag flip (Samir)
- [x] Post alert follow-up huddle (this doc)
- [ ] Short-lived tracing rule (Jonah)
- [ ] Serializer micro-benchmark (Priya)
- [ ] Canary experiment plan doc + runbook update (Claire)

Open questions / things to watch:
- Are we seeing increased memory churn on aggregator hosts correlated with batch size change? (Marta to confirm)
- Did any infra-level change (kernel, libc, allocator) get rolled to canary hosts between 2027-10-27 and 2027-10-29? (eng-infra check)
- Is there evidence that the client emits larger payloads only under specific UA strings / browser versions? If yes, may be a client-side bug.

References & links:
- PR with analytics change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2987
- Canary playbook (working copy): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Canary+Playbook+working+copy
- Related Jira tickets: ENG-4123 (canary alert), ENG-4187 (analytics payload v2 rollout)

Next sync:
- Quick async updates in #console-telemetry; 30-min follow-up huddle tomorrow 2027-10-30 09:00 UTC if reproductions are successful or if blocker emerges.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep debug traces short to avoid storing huge trace blobs. Use sampling and selective field redaction for PII-free traces.
- Consider adding a canary-only transformer node for heavy serialization so we can measure its isolated cost without affecting baseline path.
